scope: Theorem 9.3 (Finite marked systems) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 71-72. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Start with the single-model scheme, allowing fixed bounded named data of a fixed diagram. Let r be a prescribed, definable, isomorphism-invariant stationary type of a finite tuple in its root sort. Stationarity here includes free lifting under mixed arrows at eligible levels. For each finite n, the n-fold marked increment construction gives a working scheme Cn at sufficiently closed levels. Its objects are systems indexed by the subsets of {1, . . . , n}, with the prescribed marks and componentwise strong arrows. 71 For s ⊆ {1, . . . , n}, retaining the axes in s in their induced order gives a projection Ps : Cn −→ C|s|. Every such projection takes objects and arrows to objects and arrows, including mixed arrows, and preserves and reflects diagram equality on bounded tuples in its retained sorts. It consequently has the exact type correspondence of Proposition 9.1. The type in the root sort lying over r exists uniquely over every whole system and lifts freely. These conclusions include the projection to the base root and each single-axis projection. In a single-axis projection the upper object is all-dominated over its lower object together with the prescribed mark; forgetting other axes does not remove that assertion.
